description: ERCOT wholesale power prices around a Texas address or coordinate, or for a named settlement point: the load zone price for the location, the nearest resource nodes (generator and battery pricing points) with distance, and the trading hubs. Returns day-ahead hourly settlement point prices ($/MWh) for the last 7 days by default with daily average, max, min, peak and off-peak averages, hours over $100 and negative hours; Pro can request up to 120 days and hourly real-time averages. For a single settlement point, also returns rt15_stats: TB4 and TB2 computed from 15-minute real-time prices (captures intra-hour spikes that hourly averages wash out), 15-minute max, min, intervals over $100, over $1,000 and negative, plus a scarcity block: how many 15-minute intervals since RTC+B (2025-12-05) ERCOT's reliability deployment price adder was above zero (Pro adds the adder size and the highest-scarcity days). Use when someone asks what power costs or sells for at a location, how volatile prices are near a site, what a battery would see at a node, or which node or load zone a site settles in.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

days.description: Days of history. Default 7. Max 7 on the free tier, 120 on Pro.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

limit.description: How many nearby resource nodes. Default 6, max 15.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

settlement_point.description: ERCOT settlement point name, e.g. HB_HOUSTON, LZ_SOUTH or a resource node like FO_FORMOSG6. Use this instead of a location to get one node's full series.

name: node_prices
